story_text.value: Hey all, for the past couple of months I have been building a computational backend that let's people use the idle devices around their office/house to do distributed computing.  More recently I have been doing some benchmarking to see how it performs. I ran a financial workload on my Mac, took 297s to finish. Ran the same workload from dispatch to answer on a runpod h100 at 32.3 seconds. Wrangling the devices together (my Mac, and my wife and mine gaming computers) got to 32.7s. Most of it is in Python but am considering moving it to C++ to see how much lower it could go.

So this started out just over a week ago, could I drive around my village in my old car on the web, and its expanded into a massive map, with races, events, different cars and multiplayer.

I'm a web/app guy, backend guy, and yes I build it with Claude.

I know I shouldn't be astounded by what these Ai agents can do as of today, but here I am still amazed.

I've even got support from a Sim racing guy and built a web driver so he gets full force feedback for his rig, and it works.

Anyway, just a bit of fun!

Uses LIDAR data from the UK Gov + OpenStreetMap data to build the world. Technically, I could do the whole of England/Wales...but the data storage would be huge!

story_text.value:
Hi HN. I’ve been working on a project called Vaticin (with an i). Interested in your feedback.

Vaticin is a prediction market competition platform where only agents are allowed to make wagers. Humans can’t directly do so themselves. There’s no real-money wagering involved. Vaticin is built for competition, research, and education.

Every Monday morning, our LLM generates about 300 yes/no prediction questions across six categories: sports, finance, tech, entertainment, geopolitics, and science. The competition window runs Monday through Saturday, although some predictions won’t resolve for several weeks later. Agents take positions/allocations throughout the week, and then wagering locks on Saturday. Odds are live/dynamic and update with every new wager. Then a new competition cycle starts the next Monday.

We have a live leaderboard that refreshes as our LLM resolves prediction questions each night (with human moderation of resolutions).

Recognizing the value of existing prediction market competition platforms, we wanted to focus on forecasting models that are not only well-calibrated, but also make good market decisions and integrate game theory into their strategy. On Vaticin, agents have to decide which markets to take positions on, when to take a position, and how much to allocate. With the dynamic odds, agents have to adapt throughout the competition cycle. Vaticin measures more than raw prediction accuracy.

We built a few ways to build an agent. Beginners can use our no-code “agent builder” and choose which forecasting parameters/strategies they want to use, then Vaticin codes their agent, shows the user the code, but allows them to edit the code. I hope it will help beginners learn more about coding and AI agents. More experienced builders can connect their own agents through an API.

We added private tournaments, where users can create their own tournaments with their own prediction questions and fantasy tournaments where “captains” can recruit a team of agents from other users. Separate leaderboards.

We’re still building, and recognize the site isn’t “perfect” yet, but the weekly competitions/private tournaments/fantasy tournaments are live.

I’d really appreciate feedback on a few things:

- Is Vaticin’s market-based/gamified format different enough from existing forecasting competitions to be relevant?

- How would you score and rank agents over the long term? We use metrics like Brier score vs the market with adjustments for wager sample size. What else should we consider?

- What features would make you interested in entering an agent into the competition?

- Would private/custom tournaments be useful for classes, research groups, hackathons, or recruiting?

- How should we discourage human users from hand-picking their “autonomous” agents’ bets? For Vaticin-hosted agents we can log every code edit, but we aren’t sure how to integrate that into the agent ratings. For self-hosted agents we can’t track this at all. Any insight into how other bot leagues (poker, algo trading, etc) handle this?

Leaderboard: https://www.vaticin.ai/leaderboard

Note: Early in the competition week, the leaderboard will show many agents at or close to their starting 100,000-token balance because a lot of positions haven't been resolved yet (and tokens are deducted when a wager is made, so the leaderboard will show many agents with less than their initial 100,000 token allocation).

Markets: https://www.vaticin.ai/markets

Note: The prediction questions are only visible when the weekly competition cycle is open, so if you visit on the weekend that page may be empty. You can pull up prior weeks’ predictions to take a look.

Agent builder: https://www.vaticin.ai/build-an-agent

Everything is free right now. No ads.

Happy to answer questions. Thanks for any feedback, good or bad.

Thanks!

story_text.value:
Now that after Anthropic's IPO debut and with OpenAPI IPO in the works there is no doubt that the % of AI slop is going to increase disproportionately though this study says it has indeed gone down in 2026 since 2025 (https://tom-riley.co.uk/blog/ai-generated-content-statistics/) [The study itself seems to be an AI slop?] .

An analysis of 100 companies highlighted on YouTube found that while AI generated content accounted for 52.1% of published material, it generated only 4.9% of organic traffic. Meanwhile, original human content made up just 14.5% of volume but captured 87% of the traffic. If this is the case then how can AI labs generate revenue?

Even if we assume that the AI slop is going to raise after the IPOs, the content market is going to shrink and it will dilute the revenue for the content creators (using AI) forcing them to start marketing their AI slop to get visibility in the market. This is a very interesting trend to watch out for.

When I say AI slop content I am not meaning just about web publishing (Web slop), but also synthetic vibe coding (Code slop), data analysis (Data slop), agentic workflow (Software Engineering slop) etc.

If there are 1000 of the same kind of software/app clones (of course vibe coded) which will you buy? How does this compete with the originally human architected, designed and developed software/app? Finally I think it comes down to trust.

Please share your thoughts.

story_text.value:
Hi HN

I've always been drawn to puzzle and strategy games, and for a long time I've wanted to build a game of my own. While building my own version of battleship, I came across this idea of adding a super intelligent in-game AI which uses probability and statistics to reason with the board and fire its next shot.

The goal was to create a set of rules & logic capable of consistently outperforming human players, much like chess engines that have evolved to surpass even the world's strongest human chess players.

Thus I created WraithAI and named the game as Ghostfleet. WraithAI features:

1. Monte Carlo Simulation with Probability heatmaps: Before every turn WraithAI samples 800 possible enemy fleet configurations and aggregates them into a probability heatmap. It identifies the most likely locations of the enemy ships.

2. Bayesian Inference: After every shot it updates its beliefs and uses the information gain to draw a new heatmap. When two cells look equally likely WraithAI picks the one whose result would tell more about the hidden enemy fleet for its next turn.

3. Adaptive Strategy & defense: It adjusts its aggression based on the state of the game and has a mechanism which resists common search strategies.

I would genuinely like to know how people can find patterns in its behavior. Can you outsmart & beat WraithAI?

Ghostfleet also has multiplayer mode so you can play with your friends. There is a matchmaking component called TownSquare at the bottom through which you can share room codes with other players.

You can play directly in your browser:

1. Play against WraithAI: https://ghostfleet.in/play?mode=wraithAI

2. Ghostfleet: https://ghostfleet.in/

3. WraithAI Technical breakdown: https://ghostfleet.in/wraith-ai
